samples.summary: Underline-color '' fallback changed with no test covering it
samples.evidence: The delta changed `ctx.strokeStyle = resolveColor(style.underlineColor) ?? textColor` to `resolveStoredColor(resolveColor, style.underlineColor) ?? textColor` (paint-layout.ts:453). That is a real behavior change: pre-change an `underlineColor: ''` assigned '' to strokeStyle (silently ignored by canvas, inheriting whatever stroke color the previous pass left), post-change it falls back to the run's text color. No test exercises it: grepping `underlineColor` across packages/docs finds hits only in src (types.ts, text-editor.ts, paint-layout.ts) and never in test/. The added #728 tests cover only text color (paint-layout.test.ts 'renderRun cleared text color'), list markers (render-list-marker.test.ts), table cell text/markers (table-renderer.test.ts) and the helper itself (model/color.test.ts) — none set `underlineColor`. paint-layout.test.ts already has a stroke-recording ctx (`makeStrokeCtx`, asserts `s.color`), so a test would be cheap.

samples.summary: Preset-fill stubs do not reproduce the canvas 'ignores invalid color' semantics they claim; the derived negative assertions are vacuous
samples.evidence: Both new stubs are pre-loaded with a leftover fill (`SELECTION_FILL` in table-renderer.test.ts:19/makeFillStyleCtx, `PREVIOUS_FILL` in render-list-marker.test.ts:9-10) and their comments claim this "reproduces that inheritance" of issue #728. It does not: the setters store assignments verbatim, so a pre-fix `ctx.fillStyle = ''` would record `''`/`hi:` rather than retaining the preset. Consequently `expect(fills).not.toContain(`hi:${SELECTION_FILL}`)` (table-renderer.test.ts ~line 404) and the `ctx.fillStyle = PREVIOUS_FILL` line in render-list-marker.test.ts are inert — true regardless of the fix. The positive assertions (`toContain(`hi:${Theme.defaultColor}`)`, `expect(calls[0].fillStyle).toBe(Theme.defaultColor)`) do discriminate, so the tests are still meaningful; only the inheritance framing/negative assertions are noise, and a stub that ignored invalid assignments (keeping the previous value) would model the real failure.

finding.summary: renderListMarker's `?? → ||` change has no test exercising an empty-string marker color

No test passes `marker: { color: '' }` or `inline: { color: '' }`, so a regression back to `??` (marker painted in the stale fillStyle, the exact #728 failure mode) would keep the suite green. The task doc itself checks off '`renderListMarker` marker color' under the fix but lists no test for it (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:35,37-40).

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test exercises an empty-string marker/inline color for renderListMarker. packages/docs/test/view/render-list-marker.test.ts contains three such tests: line 108-114 uses `marker: { color: '' }` (with a stale PREVIOUS_FILL pre-set on the recording ctx at :110) and asserts fillStyle === Theme.defaultColor; line 116-122 does the same for `inline: { color: '' }`; line 124-139 asserts the empty string is normalized to `undefined` BEFORE reaching the resolver (`expect(seen).toEqual([undefined])`) and that the resolver's no-color branch value is painted. These are non-vacuous: the production path (paint-layout.ts:555) is `resolveStoredColor(resolveColor, colorSource) ?? theme.defaultColor`, and resolveStoredColor (model/color.ts:45-50) is what collapses ''. A regression to a bare `resolveColor(colorSource) ?? theme.defaultColor` would yield fillStyle === '' (defaultColorResolver returns strings verbatim, color.ts:14-16), failing the assertions at :113 and :121, and moving normalization after the resolver would fail :137. The tests live in the docs package whose `test` script is plain `vitest --run` (package.json:36), so they run under the default include.
